correctness.rationale: At M_n={unit zero-sum normals}, n>=3, the sparse normal p_n=(1,-1,0...)/sqrt(2) and its normalized collective tangent define a unit-speed geodesic. The Fourier section integral factorizes into two large nonzero coordinates and (n-2) equal small ones. Taylor-expanding the two large factors under an integrable majorant gives I_0=pi sqrt(2)/4 and I_2/I_0=(n-8)/(2n) by beta integrals. The remaining small-coordinate tail yields E(s)=4|s|³ int_0^infty[(1+bu²)^-(n-2)-1+(n-2)bu²]/u⁴ du + O_n(s⁴); positivity follows from convexity, two integrations by parts evaluate C_n=64(n-1)Gamma(n-1/2)/(3 sqrt(pi) n^(3/2)sqrt(n-2)Gamma(n)). In dimension 8, C_8=1001/(1024sqrt3)>0; the transverse direction has -3s²/2+o(s²), proving a saddle and C²-not-C³ collective profile. Fresh high-precision quadratures for n=3,5,8,10 at shrinking s approach all predicted C_n, corroborating but not proving asymptotic.
